instruction: Download the image from "https://huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_osworld_file_cache/resolve/main/multi_apps/3c8f201a-009d-4bbe-8b65-a6f8b35bb57f/kingbird.jpeg" and use GIMP to crop it to a square (1200x1200 pixels) and save as "square_bird.jpeg" on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "alt", "t"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires downloading image, cropping to square dimensions 1200x1200, and saving. Custom metric verifies exact dimensions.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator only verifies final image dimensions (1200x1200) but does not verify the image was downloaded from the specified URL
Cannot verify that the correct source image (kingbird.jpeg) was actually used - an agent could create any 1200x1200 image and pass
Does not verify that GIMP was actually used to perform the crop operation
Does not verify that the image was actually cropped from the original source rather than created fresh
Incomplete coverage: instruction has 5 requirements (download from URL, use GIMP, crop to square, correct dimensions, save with filename) but only dimensions and filename/location are verified
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add image content verification by comparing the cropped image against a reference crop of the source image (e.g., using perceptual hashing or pixel comparison)
Consider adding a getter to verify the source image was downloaded to a temporary location first
Add verification that the image content matches the expected kingbird image (not just dimensions)
Alternatively, simplify the instruction to only require creating a 1200x1200 image without specifying the source, if content verification is not feasible
